sections.heading: How much Hevy costs
body: Hevy is free to download, and the free version lets you log as many workouts as you like. It keeps up to 4 routines and 7 custom exercises and shows charts for the last 3 months.
Hevy Pro removes those limits for $2.99 a month, $23.99 a year or $74.99 once. Pro also adds Hevy Trainer, which builds a program for you.

If you want more, LiftCamp Pro is $9.99 a year, $1.99 a month or $29.99 once. It tells you what to lift next time, gives you a starting weight on every exercise, adds warm-up sets and a plate calculator, and removes the limit on your own routines and exercises.

sections.heading: Where Hevy is the better pick
body: Hevy runs on almost everything, including Android, Apple Watch, Wear OS and the web. LiftCamp is iPhone only for now.
Hevy also has a large social side, with a feed, followers and leaderboards. If training alongside friends who already use Hevy matters to you, that's hard to beat.
And its free version is generous. You can log as many workouts as you like, with charts covering the last 3 months.

sections.heading: Where LiftCamp is the better pick
body: LiftCamp is built for people who are new to the gym. Every exercise page tells you what weight to start with, the mistakes to watch for and what to do if the machine is taken. Hevy shows you how an exercise looks, and LiftCamp also tells you how heavy to go on day one.
You also start with a plan. LiftCamp has 31 ready-made routines, from a 2-day full body routine to push pull legs, all free. Hevy's free version lets you save up to 4 routines.
And your history stays yours. Logging, your full workout history and your PRs are free in LiftCamp and always will be.

sections.heading: Switching from Hevy
body: LiftCamp imports your Hevy history. Export your workouts from Hevy as a CSV file, then open LiftCamp and go to Settings, then Your data, then Import workouts.

Your workouts and sets come across with their real dates, so your PRs, progress charts, strength levels and streak medals pick them up straight away. LiftCamp matches each exercise to its own library, and you choose a match or skip any it isn't sure about.

Importing is free and needs a free LiftCamp account. Routines don't come across, so pick one of LiftCamp's or save your own after your first workout. If you change your mind, you can remove imported workouts in Settings without touching anything you logged in LiftCamp.

sections.heading: Which one should you use?
body: If you already know your way around the gym and want the most features, or you need Android or a watch app, Hevy is a great choice.
If you're in your first few months and want to know what to do, how much to lift and what to swap when a machine is busy, start with LiftCamp.

faq.q: Is Hevy free?
faq.a: Yes, Hevy has a free version with unlimited workouts, up to 4 routines, 7 custom exercises and 3 months of charts. Hevy Pro removes the limits for $2.99 a month, $23.99 a year or $74.99 lifetime.

faq.q: Can I import my Hevy workouts into LiftCamp?
faq.a: Yes. Export your workouts from Hevy as a CSV file, then import it in LiftCamp under Settings, Your data, Import workouts. It's free with a LiftCamp account.

faq.q: How much is Hevy Pro?
faq.a: Hevy Pro is $2.99 a month, $23.99 a year or $74.99 for a lifetime plan on the US App Store.

faq.q: Is LiftCamp free?
faq.a: Yes. Logging, full workout history, PRs, the exercise library and all 31 routines are free. LiftCamp Pro is optional at $9.99 a year, $1.99 a month or $29.99 once.

faq.q: Is there a free alternative to Hevy?
faq.a: Yes. LiftCamp is free on iPhone, with logging, full workout history, PRs and 31 ready-made routines included. Its Pro plan is $9.99 a year, less than half of Hevy Pro's yearly price.

faq.q: Is Hevy good for beginners?
faq.a: It's easy to use, but it doesn't tell you how heavy to go on each exercise. LiftCamp gives you a routine, a starting weight and form notes for each exercise.

faq.q: Is LiftCamp on Android?
faq.a: Not yet. LiftCamp is on iPhone today, and Android is coming soon.

pages.title: Best Workout App for Beginners (2026): 6 Apps Compared
pages.description: The best workout apps for beginners, compared on price, what's free and who each suits. LiftCamp, Nike Training Club, Boostcamp, Hevy, Strong and Fitbod.
pages.h1: The best workout apps for beginners
pages.lead: A beginner needs a routine to follow and an idea of how heavy to start. LiftCamp gives you both for free on iPhone, and it's our pick for your first six months in a gym. Nike Training Club is the best free choice for home workouts, and Boostcamp suits beginners who want a barbell program. We make LiftCamp, so we've listed what each of the others does better.

sections.heading: What a beginner needs from a workout app
body: A plan you can repeat. Doing the same exercises each week is how you see yourself get stronger, so an app should hand you a routine instead of a blank page.
A starting point for every exercise. Most beginners don't know how heavy to go on day one, and many apps leave that to you.
A price you'll keep paying. The best app is the one you still open in month three, and a free version means you can find out before you spend anything.

sections.heading: LiftCamp, best for your first six months
body: LiftCamp is built for people new to the gym. You pick one of 31 ready-made routines, from a 2-day full body routine to push pull legs, and each exercise tells you what weight to start with, what usually goes wrong and what to swap in when the machine is taken.
Logging, full workout history, PRs and every routine are free. LiftCamp Pro is $9.99 a year and tells you what to lift next time, with warm-up sets and a plate calculator.
It's iPhone only for now, with Android coming soon.

sections.heading: Nike Training Club, best for home workouts
body: Nike Training Club is free, with no in-app purchases. It has trainer-led video workouts and multi-week programs, many of them with no equipment, so it suits people starting at home.
It's built around classes you follow along with, so it suits home training more than logging your weights at the gym.

sections.heading: Boostcamp, best for a barbell program
body: Boostcamp's free version includes a large library of programs, including well-known beginner barbell programs, plus a tracker. Pro is $14.99 a month or $59.99 a year and adds deeper analytics and exclusive coach programs.
It suits beginners who already know the main barbell lifts and want to run a specific program.

sections.heading: Hevy, best free tracker for training with friends
body: Hevy's free version logs unlimited workouts, keeps 4 routines and shows 3 months of charts. Its feed and followers make it easy to train alongside friends. Hevy Pro is $2.99 a month, $23.99 a year or $74.99 once.
It shows you how each exercise looks, and on the free version you choose your own weights.

sections.heading: Strong, best for a fast log
body: Strong has one of the quickest logging screens around. The free version keeps 3 routines, and Strong PRO is $4.99 a month, $29.99 a year or $99.99 once.
It works best when you already have a plan to follow.

sections.heading: Fitbod, best if you want every workout planned
body: Fitbod picks the exercises, sets and weights for each session, so you never decide what to do next. There's no free version. It's $15.99 a month or $95.99 a year after a 7-day trial.
Because the workout changes each session, it can be harder to track progress on the same lifts from week to week.

faq.q: What is the best workout app for beginners?
faq.a: For gym beginners, we recommend LiftCamp, which gives you a ready-made routine and a starting weight on every exercise for free on iPhone. We make LiftCamp. For home workouts, Nike Training Club is free and has video classes.

faq.q: Is there a free workout app for beginners?
faq.a: Yes. LiftCamp, Nike Training Club, Boostcamp, Hevy and Strong all have free versions. Nike Training Club has no paid plan at all. Fitbod is the only app here with no free version.

faq.q: What's the best strength training app for beginners?
faq.a: Pick one that gives you a routine to repeat each week and tells you how heavy to start. LiftCamp does both for free. Boostcamp is a good fit if you want to run a barbell program you already know.

faq.q: Do beginners need a paid workout app?
faq.a: No. A free app with a routine you repeat each week is enough for your first months. Paid plans mostly add suggestions, charts and limits removed.
